pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Severe Ergotism (St. Anthony's Fire) secondary to CYP3A4 Drug Interaction THE SMOKING GUN: Concomitant use of prescribed ergotamine tartrate (for chronic migraines) with itraconazole (a potent CYP3A4 inhibitor for fungal infection), causing severe ergot toxicity due to completely blocked hepatic clearance. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: Ergotamine is a powerful agonist at 5-HT1B/1D serotonin and alpha-1 adrenergic receptors, triggering intense vasospasm of vascular smooth muscle. Under normal conditions, ergotamine undergoes extensive first-pass metabolism by the hepatic cytochrome P450 system (CYP3A4). When a patient receives a strong CYP3A4 inhibitor such as itraconazole, ergotamine clearance is severely impaired, causing serum drug levels to rise to toxic levels. This manifests as relentless, widespread arterial vasospasm leading to peripheral ischemia/gangrene, alongside central nervous system effects (hallucinations, seizures) driven by serotonergic and dopaminergic overstimulation.
